'''Büchi arithmetic''' of base ''k'' is the [[first-order predicate calculus|first-order theory]] of the [[natural number]]s with [[addition]] and the function <math>V_k(x)</math> which is defined as the largest power of ''k'' dividing ''x'', named in honor of the Swiss mathematician [[Julius Richard Büchi]]. The [[signature (mathematical logic)|signature]] of Büchi arithmetic contains only the addition operation, <math>V_k</math> and equality, omitting the multiplication operation entirely.

Unlike [[Peano arithmetic]], Büchi arithmetic is a [[Decidability (logic)|decidable theory]]. This means it is possible to effectively determine, for any sentence in the language of Büchi arithmetic, whether that sentence is provable from the axioms of Büchi arithmetic.

==Büchi arithmetic and automata==
A subset <math>X\subseteq \mathbb  N^n</math> is definable in Büchi arithmetic of base ''k'' if and only if it is [[Automatic sequence|''k''-recognisable]].

If <math>n=1</math> this means that the set of integers of ''X'' in base ''k'' is accepted by an [[automata theory|automaton]]. Similarly if <math>n>1</math> there exists an automaton that reads the first digits, then the second digits, and so on, of ''n'' integers in base ''k'', and accepts the words if the ''n'' integers are in the relation&nbsp;''X''.

==Properties of Büchi arithmetic==

If ''k'' and ''l'' are [[multiplicative independence|multiplicatively dependent]], then the Büchi arithmetics of base ''k'' and ''l'' have the same expressivity. Indeed <math>V_l</math> can be defined in <math>\text{FO}(V_k,+)</math>, the first-order theory of <math>V_k</math> and <math>+</math>.

Otherwise, an arithmetic theory with ''both'' <math>V_k</math> and <math>V_l</math> functions is equivalent to [[Peano axioms|Peano arithmetic]], which has both addition and multiplication, since multiplication is definable in <math>\text{FO}(V_k,V_l,+)</math>.

Further, by the [[Automatic sequence#Properties|Cobham–Semënov theorem]], if a relation is definable in both ''k'' and ''l'' Büchi arithmetics, then it is definable in [[Presburger arithmetic]].<ref>{{cite journal | first=Alan | last=Cobham | title=On the base-dependence of sets of numbers recognizable by finite automata | journal=Math. Systems Theory | volume=3 | year=1969 | issue=2 | pages=186–192 | doi=10.1007/BF01746527 | s2cid=19792434 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | first=A. L. | last=Semenov | title=Presburgerness of predicates regular in two number systems | language=Russian | journal=Sibirsk. Mat. Zh. | volume=18 | year=1977 | pages=403–418 }}</ref>
